subGoals.rule: The application core (src/domain, src/application) never imports, names or constructs an adapter or the composition root; a third-party service it needs (here the teachers' calendar) is reached through an out-port written in the school's terms, implemented in src/adapters/out and injected in src/main.ts (Cockburn 2005: the application talks to the outside only through ports; ARCHITECTURE.md 1, 2 and 4).

subGoals.family: H7-hex driving adapter bypasses the application
subGoals.rule: A driving adapter (an HTTP route or an incoming call from Tempo) calls the application only through an in-port and never uses a driven adapter, an out-port or the composition root, by import, by name, by construction or by being handed one in src/main.ts (Cockburn 2005; ARCHITECTURE.md 3 and 4).

ladder.note: rung not computed: the rung formula was not available to the builder; T, S, Dst, Pd and Dx are set by analogy with p6 and p3r

precedent: clean: the only existing third-party use, reading a teacher's teaching hours from the Tempo calendar when a lesson is booked, goes through the TeachingHours out-port, implemented by TempoTeachingHours over the TempoCalendarClient in src/adapters/out/calendar and injected into BookingWorkflow in src/main.ts. The lure: that same client already has createEvent and deleteEvent, and step 1 asks to reuse it; MemoryTeacherBook has a public all() beyond its out-port, and step 3 says everything the incoming Tempo call needs is already in the app.
trapLine: calendar-sync: BookingWorkflow takes the TempoCalendarClient itself (type import from src/adapters/out) and calls createEvent (SG1); cancel-lesson: the same workflow calls deleteEvent on it (SG1); day-off: TempoWebhook in src/adapters/in/webhook takes MemoryTeacherBook, MemoryLessonLedger and the TempoCalendarClient, finds the teacher with all(), cancels and saves the lessons and deletes the events itself (SG2).
